raw_segments.text: And there is perhaps no unimportant difference between conceiving of the chief good as in
possession or as in use, in other words, as a mere state or as a working.
For the state or habit may possibly exist in a subject without affecting any good, as,
for instance, in him who is asleep or in any other way inactive.
But the working cannot so, for it will of necessity act and act well.
And as at the Olympic Games it is not the finest and strongest men who are crowned,
but they who enter the lists, for out of these the prize men are selected.
So too in life, of the honorable and the good, it is they who act who rightly win the prizes.
